subtitle: Stone Without Mortar, City Without Fear

panels.shot: vast aerial wide over rugged ring of hills encircling a basin city
panels.action: Lines of Rajgir’s Cyclopean Wall Builders strain as they lever huge rough stones into a snaking wall that clings to the stony ridges around a green valley where smoky huts and halls cluster below.

dialogue.text: In the sixth century before the Mauryas, unknown hands ringed Rajagriha’s hills with forty kilometres of dry stone wall — a monument to fear, skill and a new age of cities.

i18n.hi: मौर्य से भी पहले, छठी सदी में, अनजाने हाथों ने राजगृह की पहाड़ियों पर चालीस किलोमीटर सूखी पत्थर की दीवार खड़ी की — डर, कौशल और नए नगरों का स्मारक।

panels.shot: low sweeping wide through a rocky mountain pass at dawn
panels.action: The camera glides between steep, scrub-covered hills of Rajgir as mists pool in the bowl-like valley, faint smoke plumes rising from scattered early houses within.

dialogue.text: The texts call it Girivraja, the hill-enclosure. A basin caught in rocky arms, where early Magadha gathered people, power and fear into one guarded hollow.

i18n.hi: ग्रंथ इसे गिरिव्रज कहते हैं, पर्वत–घेरा। पत्थरों की बाँहों में थामा कटोरा, जहाँ आरंभिक मगध ने लोग, शक्ति और डर एक ही सुरक्षित खोखले में समेट दिए।

panels.shot: medium wide on workers and overseers marking a route along a ridge
panels.action: Rajgir’s Cyclopean Wall Builders stand on a jagged ridge, one kneeling to scratch a line in the dust while another points around the curve of the hills, the valley city small below them.

dialogue.text: To guard a hollow city, the rulers of early Magadha turned to the heights. Not with brick and lime, but with raw hill-stone itself, they traced a long, unbroken line around their world.

i18n.hi: खोखले शहर की रक्षा को आरंभिक मगध के शासक ऊँचाइयों पर चढ़े। ईंट–चूने से नहीं, कच्ची पहाड़ी चट्टान से ही अपने जगत के चारों ओर लंबी, बिना टूटन की रेखा खींच दी।

panels.shot: close-up on hands testing two rough stones together
panels.action: Calloused hands of a builder press two uneven boulders together, tilting and sliding them until they lock, the gap between them narrow, the background a slope littered with more stones.

dialogue.text: Modern scholars call it a cyclopean wall. No mortar, no dressed faces. Only great undressed stones, leaned and locked so that weight and patience took the place of cement.

i18n.hi: आधुनिक विद्वान इसे चक्रनेत्री दीवार कहते हैं। न गारा, न तराशी सतह। बस बड़े–बड़े अनगढ़ पत्थर, ऐसे टिकाए–फँसाए कि भार और धीरज ही गारे की जगह बन गए।

panels.shot: wide shot of quarrying on a hillside
panels.action: Dozens of Rajgir’s Cyclopean Wall Builders wedge wooden levers under a huge rock outcrop, some pouring water into cracks, others guiding loose stones down a rough ramp.

dialogue.text: The hills themselves became the quarry. Stone prised from ledges, rolled and slid along earthen ramps, turned from wild rock into measured defence across many seasons.

i18n.hi: पहाड़ ही खदान बन गए। कगारों से पत्थर उखाड़े गए, मिट्टी की ढलानों पर लुढ़काए–घिसकाए गए, कई ऋतुओं में जंगली चट्टान से नाप–तौल कर बनाई रक्षा बना दी गई।

panels.shot: dynamic low-angle of men hauling a monolith with ropes
panels.action: Straining builders haul a massive block up a slope with thick ropes, muscles taut, bare feet digging into dust, while a foreman gestures toward the rising spine of wall ahead.

dialogue.text: There is no inscription naming a king. Only the labour remembers. In the second urbanisation, when mahajanapadas grew and war hardened, such walls were the new grammar of power.

i18n.hi: किसी राजा का नाम खुदा नहीं। बस श्रम की याद बची है। द्वितीय नगरयुग में, जब महाजनपद बढ़े और युद्ध कठोर हुआ, ऐसी दीवारें शक्ति की नई भाषा बन गईं।

panels.shot: high oblique shot along a completed segment of wall
panels.action: The camera rides above a freshly completed stretch of thick stone wall marching along a ridge, its uneven top dotted with watch platforms, a narrow path running just inside it.

dialogue.text: Stone by stone, the line grew. Some stretches thick, some thin, hugging the contours, adjusting to ravines and saddles, built not in one sweep but in phases over generations.

i18n.hi: पत्थर–पत्थर जोड़कर रेखा बढ़ती गई। कहीं मोटी, कहीं पतली, धरती की मोड़–रेखाएँ पकड़ती, घाटियों–दर्रों के हिसाब से ढलती, एक ही झटके में नहीं, कई पीढ़ियों में चरण–चरण बनी।

panels.shot: medium on builders examining a sherd of Northern Black Polished Ware
panels.action: A builder crouches by a fire, holding up a glossy black pottery sherd while others sit around, a pile of such sherds beside an embankment near the wall line.

dialogue.text: Beneath some stretches, archaeologists later found Northern Black Polished Ware. Fine tableware of an early city elite, telling us the first major wall belonged to a pre-Mauryan Magadha.

i18n.hi: कुछ हिस्सों के नीचे पुरातत्वविदों को बाद में उत्तरी काली पालिशदार मृद्भांड मिला। शुरुआती नगर अभिजातों का बढ़िया बर्तन, जो बताता है कि पहली बड़ी दीवार मौर्य–पूर्व मगध की थी।

panels.shot: twilight wide of guarded gate cutting between two hills
panels.action: At dusk, a narrow stone-lined pass between two ridges is closed by a stout wooden gate inset into the wall, torches flickering as a few armed sentries stand alert.

dialogue.text: Buddhist texts remember Rajagriha as a guarded hill city. Gates in the passes, sentries on the ridges. To enter, one climbed and was watched. The enclosure itself was a weapon.

i18n.hi: बौद्ध ग्रंथ राजगृह को संरक्षित पर्वत–नगर के रूप में याद रखते हैं। दर्रों पर फाटक, कगारों पर पहरा। भीतर आने को चढ़ना पड़ता, और नज़रें पीछा करतीं। खुद घेरा ही हथियार था।

panels.shot: wide view of city inside basin with wall cresting above
panels.action: From within the valley, huts, halls, and small shrines cluster along paths, smoke rising, while beyond them the stone wall crowns the surrounding hills, sentries tiny against the sky.

dialogue.text: Inside, life thickened. Assemblies, markets, rituals. Outside, rival powers watched. The wall spoke for the city: this basin has a ruler, an army, a will to stand behind stone.

i18n.hi: भीतर जीवन घना हुआ। सभाएँ, बाज़ार, अनुष्ठान। बाहर प्रतिद्वंदी शक्तियाँ ताकती रहीं। दीवार शहर की ओर से बोलती रही: इस कटोरे का शासक है, सेना है, और पत्थर के पीछे टिकने की इच्छा है।

panels.shot: montage-like wide with ghosted silhouettes of rival states beyond hills
panels.action: Beyond the ring of hills, faint superimposed silhouettes of other fortified towns and banners hint at distant Kashi, Kosala and Vajji, while storm clouds gather on the horizon.

dialogue.text: This was the age of mahajanapadas. Kashi and Kosala to the west, Vajji to the north, Anga to the east. In this jostling field, early Magadha armed its capital with stone.

i18n.hi: यह महाजनपदों का युग था। पश्चिम में काशी और कोसल, उत्तर में वज्जि, पूरब में अंग। इस धक्कामुक्की के मैदान में आरंभिक मगध ने अपनी राजधानी को पत्थर से सुसज्जित किया।

panels.shot: medium on a Buddhist monk looking up at the wall from a path
panels.action: A robed monk walks along a path skirting the wall, pausing to look up at its massive stones, the valley opening beyond him, his expression thoughtful.

dialogue.text: Later texts recall great conflicts with the Vajji confederacy and the guarding of approaches. The details blur, but always the image returns: a hill city, enclosed and wary.

i18n.hi: बाद के ग्रंथ वज्जि संघ से बड़े संघर्षों और मार्ग–रक्षा को याद करते हैं। विवरण धुँधले हैं, पर छवि लौट आती है: पहाड़ी नगर, घिरा हुआ और सतर्क।

panels.shot: medium close on an older builder resting against the wall
panels.action: An older builder sits with his back to the wall stones, sweat-darkened, gazing out over the valley as younger workers carry smaller stones toward a repair in the distance.

dialogue.speaker: rajgir_s_cyclopean_wall_builders
dialogue.text: We build, and others will patch and raise again. The wall never ends.

i18n.hi: हम बनाएँगे, और कोई आगे चलकर जोड़ेगा, ऊँचा करेगा। दीवार का काम कभी पूरा नहीं होता।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide showing subtle changes in the wall over centuries
panels.action: The same stretch of wall is shown as vegetation creeps, some stones sag, then later smaller, neatly cut stones are added atop, hinting at different building phases under changing skies.

dialogue.text: The record suggests later hands altered and repaired the barrier. Some courses coarser, some more regular. The wall, like the city, was not fixed but layered by time.

i18n.hi: लेख बताता है कि बाद के हाथों ने इस घेरे को बदला–सँवारा। कहीं गच्चे मोटे, कहीं पंक्तियाँ करीने से। दीवार भी, शहर की तरह, स्थिर नहीं रही, समय की तहों से बनी।

panels.shot: modern-era wide shot of the ruined wall snaking over green hills
panels.action: Centuries later, the weathered remnants of the wall snake over lush green hills, some stretches broken, others intact, as a lone modern figure in the distance walks along its crest.

dialogue.text: Today only fragments remain, listed and measured by surveys, their circuit traced roughly at forty kilometres. Parts have fallen, but the idea still arcs across the hills.

i18n.hi: आज बस कुछ टुकड़े बचे हैं, सर्वेक्षणों में दर्ज–नापा हुआ, जिनकी परिक्रमा लगभग चालीस किलोमीटर आँकी गई। हिस्से ढह गए, पर विचार आज भी पहाड़ियों पर धनुष की तरह छाया है।

panels.shot: close-up on interlocked stones, plants growing in crevices
panels.action: A tight view on two large, irregular stones wedged together, tiny plants sprouting from narrow gaps, the texture of the rock rough and enduring.

dialogue.text: There are no cement seams to study. Only the meeting of stone with stone, the craft of fitting irregular faces so that gravity, not mortar, keeps the past standing.

i18n.hi: यहाँ गारे की जोड़–रेखाएँ पढ़ने को नहीं। बस पत्थर से पत्थर की भेंट है, टेढ़े–मेढ़े चेहरों को ऐसा जड़ने की कारीगरी कि गारा नहीं, गुरुत्वाकर्षण अतीत को खड़ा रखे।

panels.shot: wide contemplative shot of the wall and the valley at sunset
panels.action: At sunset, the camera looks from the wall down into the Rajgir basin, now layered with later ruins and greenery, the stone line catching the last light along the ridge.

dialogue.text: A wall records both fear and organisation. Around Rajagriha, this dry-stone ring marks a moment when a hill basin chose to become a capital, binding its fate to stone and to history.

i18n.hi: दीवार डर और संगठन, दोनों लिखती है। राजगृह के चारों ओर यह सूखी पत्थर की अंगूठी वह क्षण दर्ज करती है जब एक पहाड़ी कटोरे ने राजधानी बनने का फैसला किया, और अपने भाग्य को पत्थर और इतिहास से बाँध लिया।

title_i18n.en: The Forty Kilometre Wall Without Mortar
title_i18n.hi: बिना गारे की चालीस किलोमीटर दीवार

subtitle_i18n.en: Stone Without Mortar, City Without Fear
subtitle_i18n.hi: पत्थर बिना गारे, शहर बिना डर
